title: The year in one sitting
hookLine: Abhidhamma, the sutras, Zen, Pure Land, Tibet, the movements, the practices

lines: A MAN ASLEEP UNDER A TREE.
cards: A man is asleep under a mango tree. A ripe mango thumps down beside his head. He wakes, opens his eyes, reaches out, picks it up, squeezes it, smells it, and eats it.

That little scene, a commentary's simile for how a single moment of seeing unfolds, is near where this year began. Today, one sitting for the whole year, from the falling mango to the full moon of the heart.

teach.b: It began with the Abhidhamma: the mind taken apart into moments, each arising and passing, colored by factors, held up by roots.
Then the great vehicle: the bodhisattva, who seeks waking for the sake of all, and the perfections of giving, ethics, patience, effort, meditation and wisdom.
The Diamond Sutra opened on an ordinary morning: the Buddha dresses, walks for alms, eats, washes his feet and sits down.
The Lotus gave you a burning house, a jewel sewn into a sleeping man's coat, a doctor who seemed to leave.
Vimalakirti lay sick in a small room that somehow held seats for a whole assembly, and answered a question with silence.
Zen and Chan: a straight back, thumbs just touching, breaths counted to ten, and an ox searched for, caught, ridden home, forgotten, until a man walks into the market with open hands.

teach.h: ZEN, PURE LAND, TIBET, THE MOVEMENTS.
teach.b: Pure Land: a monk named Dharmakara making vows for a land where all can wake, with birds whose songs are the teaching.
Tibet: the ancient ones and the whispered lineage, Milarepa, sending and taking on the breath, monks debating in a courtyard with a clap and a stamp.
Other schools and movements: Tiantai and Huayan, the golden lion, Ambedkar's new vehicle, practice put to work for peace and the earth.
The schools side by side: the arahant and the bodhisattva, each honored in its own home.
The practice traditions: chanting in Pali and to a wooden drum, bowing, a ten-day retreat, a pilgrimage. The festivals: a lamp, a footprint, a pinch of barley, a monk in a pine tree.
School after school, each in its own words.

how: Some Buddhist communities close a period of study with a longer sitting and a look back over what was taught, ending with a dedication of merit to all beings.

games.q: what does “the year in one sitting” mean?
o: a twenty-minute test on year four's facts
one short sitting that looks back over year four
the last festival of the Buddhist year

games.q: the year in pictures: tap the pairs.

s: this year began with the Zen ox pictures
it began with the Abhidhamma, the mind in moments, and the mango simile.
in the Diamond Sutra's opening, the Buddha washes his feet and sits down
an ordinary morning: dressing, alms, eating, washing, sitting.
in the ox pictures, the man ends by walking into the market with open hands
after the ox and the self are forgotten.

games.q: you're asleep under a mango tree, and a ripe mango thumps down by your head. in the commentary's simile, what comes next?
o: you wake, pick it up, smell it, and eat it.
you shout for the owner of the tree.
games.why: he wakes, reaches out, picks it up, squeezes it, smells it and eats it: one moment of seeing, step by step.

practice: Let a few schools pass through one short sitting: back straight and thumbs just touching, the way Zen sits, and a few out-breaths counted, one to ten.

Notice one moment of mind arise and pass, the way the Abhidhamma watches, and, if it feels right, breathe in someone's trouble and breathe out ease, as the Tibetan block taught. Then drop every method and just sit.

wordCard.voice: The year in one sitting. Year four, seen whole: the Abhidhamma, the great sutras, Zen, Pure Land, Tibet, the movements, the practices and the festivals. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: look how far. A mango, a burning house, an ox, a bird, a clap in a courtyard. Tomorrow, the year closes.
